treatment.logline: In a rain-bound Colombo garage, Nimal turns a financial proposal into a personal challenge, leaving Dinu holding a key but withholding his agreement.

arc.beat: Return six hours and expose the material
The financial argument meets a moral boundary

treatment.approach: A tight handheld scene with restrained drift, not agitation. The intended cut moves from shared space to opposing singles, then returns to shared geography for the handoff. Because the source action is brief, the approximately 120-second bin is essential editorial coverage of the same moments, not 120 seconds of new events. Full-line masters, singles and silent receiving angles give the editor control of pauses without extending or rewriting dialogue.

treatment.geography: Nimal stands frame left facing right; Dinu stands frame right facing left throughout. The camera remains on the entrance side of their axis. Nimal supports the metal box in his left hand and opens it with his right; the open lid stays raised. He later lifts C-17 with his right hand and releases it into Dinu's open right palm. No hand touches another hand.
treatment.key_image: Dinu's lowered gaze above his still-open right palm, with Nimal separated at the left edge of the shared frame.
advice: Add the English temporal caption in post over the opening shared frame; do not request generated lettering.
Photographs and bank documents must be identifiable as categories, never supplied with invented readable facts.
Hold resistance and the final gaze without a confirming nod or a closing fist.
The full-length spoken coverage is raw material for alternate picture choices, not an instruction to repeat lines in the edit.

sequences.purpose: Let Dinu's objection land before Nimal applies personal pressure.

sequences.purpose: Show the key's transfer and leave Dinu's decision open.

moments.cut_uses: Start with the shared master and favour Nimal's eye-level single; the full-duration receiving single allows the allegation to land off screen.

moments.what: Dinu challenges the proposal in L3.
moments.cut_uses: Dinu's eye-level single is the hinge; shared and receiving coverage retain the distance between friends.

moments.what: Nimal shifts to Dinu's attachment to Aruni in L4.
moments.cut_uses: Nimal's tighter single carries the entire line, with a full receiving single available for the moment the pressure registers.

moments.what: Nimal lifts C-17 from the box and releases it into Dinu's open right palm.
moments.feeling: An obligation is placed, not accepted.
moments.cut_uses: Shared waist-height master preserves donor, receiver and direction; a tighter shared view supplies a precise release without physical contact.

moments.what: Dinu studies the key as rain continues on the roof.
moments.cut_uses: Hold Dinu's single with his palm visible; shared and Nimal receiving coverage give the editor a sustained ending without inventing agreement.

editor_notes: The 114-second must bin is raw coverage for a 120-second target, not a 114-second assembly. Choose one complete performance of each line and use receiving shots under that audio; never repeat, shorten or split a line.

Masters establish the left-right axis and custody; singles carry each speaker's turn; reactions hold what lands; the tighter shared handoff supplies the release cut point. The final shared frame and Dinu single preserve the unresolved decision.

Nimal and Dinu are unplaced before their first specified positions, so both begin standing in their later established left/right positions. Dinu raises his right palm between the last personal-appeal angle and the handoff; Nimal retains the open box in his left hand throughout.

Match box lid, hand positions, key direction and the 1.5-second opening and transfer across their paired views. For the transfer, avoid skin contact and fast finger work: use the clean shared sources with a carefully concealed edit or post composite if the generated handoff fails. Do not imply a second transfer.
L4 fills almost all of an eight-second take: the 0.6-second settled lead and tail each include the 0.5-second dialogue pad. Protect them and use adjacent silent coverage for a longer pause.

Add the earlier-time caption and, if needed, the key's C-17 marking in post; do not rely on generated lettering. Keep the photographs and bank documents visually identifiable without fabricated readable particulars.
Build the roof-rain bed, breathing and restrained metal effects in post over silent picture sources. No score is required.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options, not generated camera moves; clean handheld sources are provided if post elects to use them. None is required by this cut. Keep the handoff at normal speed.
Avoid mirrors, complex finger manipulation and bodily contact in the generated material. Do not add a nod, a closed fist, a departure or any gesture that settles Dinu's choice.

editor_notes: The 114-second must bin is raw coverage for a 120-second target, not a 114-second assembly. Choose one complete performance of each line and use receiving shots under that audio; never repeat, shorten or split a line.

Masters establish the left-right axis and custody; singles carry each speaker's turn; reactions hold what lands; the tighter shared handoff supplies the release cut point. The final shared frame and Dinu single preserve the unresolved decision.

Nimal and Dinu are unplaced before their first specified positions, so both begin standing in their later established left/right positions. Dinu raises his right palm between the last personal-appeal angle and the handoff; Nimal retains the open box in his left hand throughout.

Match box lid, hand positions, key direction and the 1.5-second opening and transfer across their paired views. For the transfer, avoid skin contact and fast finger work: use the clean shared sources with a carefully concealed edit or post composite if the generated handoff fails. Do not imply a second transfer.
L4 fills almost all of an eight-second take: the 0.6-second settled lead and tail each include the 0.5-second dialogue pad. Protect them and use adjacent silent coverage for a longer pause.

Add the earlier-time caption and, if needed, the key's C-17 marking in post; do not rely on generated lettering. Keep the photographs and bank documents visually identifiable without fabricated readable particulars.
Build the roof-rain bed, breathing and restrained metal effects in post over silent picture sources. No score is required.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options, not generated camera moves; clean handheld sources are provided if post elects to use them. None is required by this cut. Keep the handoff at normal speed.
Avoid mirrors, complex finger manipulation and bodily contact in the generated material. Do not add a nod, a closed fist, a departure or any gesture that settles Dinu's choice.
